**Title (English, from literature):** Bathing naked

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 21 (titled *Nagga*, "Bathing naked") is a disciplinary training rule in the Vinaya Piṭaka concerning Buddhist nuns. The rule stipulates that a nun who bathes naked commits an offense requiring expiation (*pācittiya*) [Conze 1954; Hüsken 1997]. In her analysis of the nuns' legal corpus, Ute Hüsken contrasts this explicit prohibition against naked bathing in Pācittiya 21 with Bhikkhunī Pācittiya 2, which specifically proscribes the removal of pubic hair [Hüsken 1997]. Modern translations include an English rendering by Bhikkhu Brahmali.
